newsitem.title: CANADA: Loewen off on profit-taking/long fight seen.
newsitem.headline: Loewen off on profit-taking/long fight seen.

text.p: Shares in Loewen Group Inc fell sharply on Wednesday afternoon on profit-taking as traders expected a protracted battle with hostile bidder Service Corp International.

Loewen shares were off one to 41 on their first day of trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Service stock was up 1/4 at 30-1/8. Houston-based Service said earlier today it was launching a US$45 a share stock offer for Loewen, its smaller rival in the funeral service industry.
Loewen, which said it would review the offer, was widely expected to fight Service vigorously.

Loewen last week rejected a US$43 a share bid by Service. "This looks like it could take a long time. Some of the weak hands are a little frustrated Service Corp was not more aggressive" and took profits, one trader said.
Added another trader: "People are expecting this to be long and drawn out. Some people think it's a good time to get out with a profit."

Traders expressed mild disappointment that Service's offer was not higher than US$45 a share after some investors had speculated it could be as high as US$48. But Service said it might increase its offer if Loewen were to negotiate.
Traders expected Service to increase pressure gradually on Loewen. Arbitragers said it was positive that the bid was not conditioned on achieving pooling-of-interest accounting.
"It was a mixed bag. Everyone is settling in for a long fight," said one arbitrager.
Loewen stock peaked at 42-5/8, a gain of 5/8, in early trading after the revised Service Corp bid was announced.
